item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, a faster, lower-cost AI model matching GPT-6 Luna's pricing up to 100,000 tokens with new API credits for subscribers [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Anthropic has introduced Claude Haiku 5.5, a new AI model designed to be faster and more affordable, matching the price of OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna up to 100,000 tokens but increasing costs beyond that. The model uses a less generous tokenizer, resulting in higher token counts for the same input compared to its predecessor, Haiku 4.5, which was released nearly a year ago at a significantly higher price. Alongside the model launch, Anthropic has halved the price of cache reads for Sonnet 5.5 and introduced monthly API credits for Max and Team subscribers, ranging from $100 to $500 depending on the plan. These credits match the subscription cost and aim to make API usage more accessible, with options to disable auto-reload to prevent unexpected charges. The credits do not roll over monthly, encouraging users to utilize them within the billing period.

item.title: Michael Lynch outlines common anti-patterns in software blogging, warning against meandering intros, overreliance on links, and excessive formality
item.description: Michael Lynch offers advice on software blogging pitfalls, cautioning writers against lengthy introductions, assuming readers' prior knowledge, and relying too much on links instead of explaining terms. He emphasizes that articles should be understandable even without clicking external links. Lynch also encourages bloggers to write in a natural, conversational style rather than a stiff, formal tone, noting that many developers delegating writing to AI have made software blogging bland and uniform, while readers seek more personality in writing.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 with Intelligent UI in ChatGPT, enabling interactive, visual responses for over 1.2 billion weekly users [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 in ChatGPT, featuring an Intelligent UI that delivers faster, more interactive responses combining text, visuals, and interactive elements. This update aims to make complex topics easier to understand and everyday tasks more engaging for the platform's large user base. The Intelligent UI allows ChatGPT to generate responses with graphics, buttons, forms, and charts tailored to the user's questions, enabling interactive experiences such as calculators or games directly within conversations. GPT-6 also improves response speed by beginning to answer while continuing to process information, enhancing user experience across web and mobile platforms.

item.title: Meta and Microsoft reduce employee use of Anthropic's Claude AI as they shift to proprietary coding tools [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Meta and Microsoft have started limiting their employees' use of Anthropic's Claude AI, focusing instead on their own AI coding assistants. This move aims to control internal AI spending and streamline development processes without affecting customer access to Claude through Microsoft's platforms. Microsoft has cut internal AI spending limits significantly, reducing monthly allowances from $100,000 to about $10,000 per employee in many cases, while Meta's Claude Code users dropped from around 60,000 to 30,000 amid a shift to MetaCode and Muse Code, its proprietary AI tools. Despite fewer users, Meta's spending on Claude remains substantial, reflecting ongoing demand and competition in AI development. The transition highlights the challenges of managing AI costs and security risks, as vulnerabilities in AI coding assistants have been identified and addressed. Both companies continue to invest in AI but are tightening budgets and prioritizing their own technologies amid a competitive landscape.

item.title: Researchers show AI autoformalisation in Lean may misrepresent natural language proofs, including OpenAI's Navier-Stokes blow-up claim [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new study demonstrates that translating mathematical proofs from natural language into formal languages like Lean using AI does not guarantee the original argument's correctness. The researchers highlight that resolving ambiguities in mathematical language is computationally more complex than any known problem, including the Halting problem, making faithful AI autoformalisation effectively impossible. They provide examples where AI mistranslations led to discrepancies between natural language proofs and their formal verifications, specifically pointing out that OpenAI's announced proof of blow-up solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations does not correspond accurately between the natural language and Lean formalisation.

item.title: Docker launches Docker Agent CLI plugin for building and running AI agents with YAML configs and multi-agent orchestration [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Docker Agent is a new CLI plugin that enables users to create, run, and share AI agents defined in declarative YAML configurations without coding. It supports multi-agent collaboration, integrates with various AI providers including OpenAI and Anthropic, and offers a rich ecosystem of tools and retrieval-augmented generation features. The plugin is pre-installed with Docker Desktop 4.63+ and can also be installed via Homebrew or binary releases. Users can run agents locally or from OCI registries, and the system supports both cloud API keys and local models through Docker Model Runner. Docker collects anonymous telemetry data to improve the tool and maintains community support through Docker Community Slack channels.

item.title: OpenAI publishes new mathematical results from internal frontier model with Lean proof formalizations and research details on GitHub [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has released a collection of new mathematical findings generated by an internal frontier AI model, sharing formalized proofs in the Lean programming language and detailed research data on GitHub. The release follows consultations with the Institute for Advanced Study's Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence to establish best practices for sharing AI-generated mathematical work. The GitHub repository includes protocols for paper revisions, citations, and summaries of the model's reasoning, along with compute usage estimates equivalent to about three hours of ChatGPT Pro per result. OpenAI plans to fund workshops and programs to further explore AI-produced mathematical results and aims to responsibly release the model while continuing to refine standards based on community feedback.

item.title: Researchers complete AI-assisted formal proof of optimal packing for 11 squares using Lean verification with native numerical certificates
item.description: A team has finalized a formal proof verifying the optimal packing of 11 squares, employing AI-assisted methods and the Lean proof assistant. The verification passed all checks with zero admissions, confirming the optimal side length and arrangement under specified geometric constraints. The proof and verification artifacts are publicly available, enabling reproduction and audit by others. This work builds on extensive formalization efforts and uses pinned versions of Lean and Mathlib to ensure consistency and reliability.

item.title: Coroner links Auckland man's 2024 suicide to sextortion blackmail involving AI-generated persona [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A 41-year-old man in Auckland took his own life in 2024 after being blackmailed by criminals using an AI-generated woman named "Donna Chase" to solicit and exploit sexually explicit images. The man paid money to the scammers, believed to be part of an overseas organized criminal network, before his death within hours of first contact. The coroner highlighted the man's vulnerable state amid personal stresses and warned about the dangers of sextortion scams involving AI-generated personas. Police and online safety groups advise victims not to pay blackmail demands and to seek help from organizations like Netsafe.

item.title: US DOJ sentences man to 18 months for AI-generated music streaming fraud that stole $8M in royalties, outstreaming Taylor Swift's catalog by billions [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Michael Smith, a 54-year-old North Carolina man, was sentenced to 18 months in prison after pleading guilty to using AI-generated songs and 10,000 bots to fraudulently stream music on platforms like Spotify and Apple Music. The scheme, which ran undetected for seven years, generated billions of fake streams and diverted millions in royalties from legitimate artists. Smith created hundreds of thousands of AI-generated songs and used thousands of fraudulent accounts funded by stolen debit cards to inflate streaming numbers, at times surpassing the streams of top artists such as Taylor Swift. The Department of Justice called this the first criminal case involving AI-assisted streaming fraud and ordered Smith to forfeit over $8 million in illicit gains. Despite Smith's legal team's request for probation, the court emphasized the need for deterrence against such sophisticated fraud schemes.

item.title: Discussion on public opinion reveals mixed feelings about AI, with many users expressing both support and concern amid growing skepticism [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The article discusses varying public attitudes toward artificial intelligence, highlighting a mix of support and worry among users. It notes that while some people remain optimistic about AI's benefits, others have become more skeptical or concerned, particularly about how AI is developed and deployed. The conversation reflects a broader trend in Western countries where many users simultaneously use, appreciate, and fear AI technologies.

item.title: Developer uses AI to build open source clones of Adobe Creative Cloud apps with plans for full feature parity within months [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Brandon Thomas, a software developer, has created a suite of seven open source applications that replicate Adobe's Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro using AI-powered reverse engineering. These apps, built in Rust with WebAssembly versions for browsers, are currently in an early alpha state but aim to achieve near-complete feature parity with Adobe's software within months. Thomas plans to fund development by selling token-based access to an AI model integrated into the apps, ensuring ongoing support and updates. Thomas was motivated to develop these alternatives after negative experiences with Adobe's cancellation fees and envisions a future where developers can create open source equivalents of popular paid software to reclaim control over technology. While the project is legally cautious about mimicking Adobe's trade dress, it represents a significant effort to challenge proprietary software dominance using AI tools for rapid development and clean-room reverse engineering.

item.title: Law firms report AI has not reduced legal billing rates or hours worked despite efficiency gains, with demand and review processes offsetting time savings [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Law firms have not seen a decline in legal billing rates or hours worked despite adopting AI tools, as increased demand and the need to review AI-generated work maintain or raise workloads. Most legal spending remains hourly, and many in-house lawyers report no significant cost savings from AI use. Firms are investing heavily in AI platforms but face challenges in adjusting compensation models tied to billable hours. The persistence of high billing rates and hours is attributed to factors such as increased work volume, more extensive diligence requirements, and additional review time for AI outputs. Some clients forbid AI-generated deliverables, complicating cost reductions. Ethical guidelines require lawyers to bill only actual time spent, limiting the ability to pass AI tool costs to clients without disclosure. Firms are experimenting with fixed fees and tracking AI usage to adapt to these changes. This dynamic creates tension between efficiency gains from AI and traditional legal billing practices, with firms cautious about reducing fees despite technological advances. The evolving landscape raises questions about future billing models and client expectations as AI becomes more integrated into legal workflows.

item.title: Senator Kelly's AI tax bill proposes levies on computational processing, digital ads, and excess profits but struggles to directly link AI activity to economic harms [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Senator Mark Kelly introduced the Make AI Work for Americans Act, which proposes three taxes aimed at capturing economic gains from AI and offsetting labor market harms. The bill taxes computational processing measured in data volume, digital advertising revenue, and excess profits from AI-related businesses to fund worker adjustment programs. However, the proposal faces criticism for its difficulty in clearly connecting these tax bases to the specific economic disruptions caused by AI, such as job displacement or wage impacts. The bill uses proxies like data volume and advertising revenue that may not directly reflect AI's labor market effects, raising questions about the fairness and coherence of the taxation approach.

item.title: Report: AI is being deployed to improve global food security through early warning systems, crop optimization, and guided agriculture amid rising hunger challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: AI is increasingly used to address global hunger by enhancing food security through early warning systems that monitor crops and predict crises, optimizing crop genetics, and providing farmers with precise agricultural guidance. Despite agricultural advances producing more food than ever, 2.7 billion people still cannot afford a healthy diet, and nearly 700 million face undernourishment, with pressures from conflict, climate change, and economic shocks worsening the situation. The deployment of AI builds on decades of agricultural innovation and humanitarian efforts, aiming to connect and optimize data and tools that were previously siloed. However, experts caution that AI's benefits come with risks, emphasizing the need for balanced data access, privacy, regulation, and capacity building to ensure equitable and effective use. Successful AI integration in food systems will require collaboration among technical developers, policymakers, and local stakeholders to create community-specific solutions and avoid repeating past agricultural pitfalls.

item.description: Ashish Kumar, a former AI lead for Tesla's Optimus humanoid robots, has co-founded a startup developing non-humanoid robots that handle a variety of tasks that would normally be done by highly skilled workers in industries such as manufacturing and aerospace, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The company uses reinforcement learning-a method that rewards AI for accomplishing certain goals and penalizes it for other actions-to teach robots to perform complex tasks, according to the two people. (Kumar's doctoral research at the University of California, Berkeley, focused on RL.)

item.title: Where Nvidia's $100 Billion Dealmaking Juggernaut Will Go Next [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This July, Nvidia caught wind of a looming takeover of OpenRouter, a three-year-old startup that had emerged as a popular marketplace for AI models, including many cheaper open-source ones. Databricks and Stripe had already been talking to the startup about a potential sale. Nvidia was late to the party. The chipmaker's CEO, Jensen Huang, wanted in. Nvidia executives told their counterparts at OpenRouter they were interested and were prepared to make a generous offer, but they needed more time to evaluate a possible transaction before doing so, said a person with knowledge of the discussion. OpenRouter's founders didn't want to wait. Ultimately, Nvidia-whose interest in the startup hasn't previously been reported-didn't make a formal offer, and Stripe prevailed with an $8 billion bid for OpenRouter. Nvidia's dealmakers quickly moved on to other prizes. Over the next two months, they inked more than $140 billion worth of deals-including a $105 billion credit guarantee. The company held nearly $100 billion worth of equity investments and $25 billion in future investment commitments as of late July. More deals are likely.

item.title: AI Agenda Live: From Token Maxing to Value maxing: Getting More From Every Unit of Compute [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: In AI circles, conversations about compute shortages are as common as talk of the weather. As agentic workflows threaten to multiply token consumption further, it's little wonder that talk has shifted from securing GPUs to optimizing them. At a recent panel, The Information's Phoebe Liu sat down with three AI leaders-from chipmakers and AI clouds to Fortune 500s-to discuss how they're squeezing more tokens from every unit of compute. Those on the panel were: Marc Boroditsky, Chief Revenue Officer, Nebius Mattie Toia, VP, Infrastructure, Uber Dion Harris, Sr. Director, HPC & AI Hyperscale Infrastructure Solutions, NVIDIA Optimizing to the customer's KPI Nebius was recently rated Platinum, the top tier, in SemiAnalysis' ClusterMAX rating, which puts GPU cloud providers through a suite of hands-on tests on the compute they supply. This distinction, said Chief Revenue Officer Marc Boroditsky, reflects the company's ability to deliver high performance at high efficiency. "Not only are we a well-regarded supplier for neolabs, but we're also enterprise-grade, so ready to supply the entire market," he said. He noted that Nebius tailors optimizations in Nebius Token Factory, its inference platform, to specific customer's specific goals, whether speed, reliability, quality or price. One recent example of how they do this is speculative decoding, which allows smaller models to predict likely next tokens that a larger model verifies in bulk, rather than generating one token at a time. Nebius uses each customer's own traffic to improve the result. NVIDIA, meanwhile, is helping companies avoid unnecessary compute altogether. A feature in its Dynamo platform locates already-computed data sitting in a cluster's KV cache so teams don't waste compute recalculating it. "We're seeing a lot of bang for the buck in terms of driving performance, efficiency and overall effectiveness," noted NVIDIA's Dion Harris. Uber has seen its token costs stabilize in recent months even as its use of agentic workflows has grown, said Mattie Toia. She credited caching pushed down to individual sub-agents, plus a simpler shift: giving engineers visibility into their own usage. "It starts by giving visibility to individual users-how many tokens they're spending, the relative cost of them. That gives people context to think about how they're optimizing," she said. Boroditsky described the shift as moving from "token maxing" to "value maxing": measuring how many agent turns, tokens and dollars it takes to reach an outcome, whether that's a document or a completed form. "What you're looking for is, how do I actually optimize the value that I'm creating for the cost that I'm spending?" he said. The ecosystem at work Improving the economics of compute is a job for the whole industry, not any one company, the panel agreed. "It takes a lot more than a chip to deliver AI at scale," Harris said. He pointed to compounding gains from pairing new hardware with better software-kernel tuning, smarter frameworks, and tools built across NVIDIA's ecosystem. Over a chip's lifetime, this can drive 3-5X performance gains from day zero to year five. Boroditsky added that no single model wins every use case. "Models matter a lot, but by themselves, they don't solve a problem," he said. "It's the entire end-to-end solution." Data discipline One thing companies can do today, Toia said, is get their own data in order. "There is a lot of valuable data that most organizations have that is really important to grounding your models," she said. Uber built an internal "context graph"-roughly 24 million nodes pulled from Jira tickets, system design docs and code reviews-to feed its AI agents better context, cutting query times from 20 minutes to 30 seconds while using fewer tokens. Boroditsky agreed with this approach, noting that the companies that build centralized resources get better results. His five-year prediction: "The leading companies in the market will have taken control of their intelligence." The future of pricing Asked whether Nebius would consider outcome-based pricing, Boroditsky said the company was open to the idea. "I don't think we've figured out yet the right economic model between the supplier and the customer," he said. Nebius already runs capacity auctions and recently launched spot pricing. As the applications built on Nebius move toward outcome-based models, Boroditsky noted that vendors will have to adapt. Looking ahead, he expects managed services to route workloads intelligently on customers' behalf. "In the coming quarters, you're going to see a lot more managed services that are doing more of the heavy lifting," he said.

item.title: Google says 180 billion images and videos now carry SynthID watermarks as detector goes public [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google's AI watermark detector SynthID is now public. Anyone can check whether images, videos, or audio were created by Google's AI or partners like OpenAI and Nvidia. More than 180 billion pieces of content already carry the watermark, but the tool only identifies SynthID-tagged content, not AI-generated media in general. item.title: Grab Redesigns Counter Service Storage for 50% Lower P99 Latency
item.description: Grab migrated its high-volume Counter Service from a wide column database to Aerospike using storage abstraction, shadow traffic, data parity validation, and gradual traffic migration. The redesigned data model consolidated time buckets into map-based records. Grab reports about 50% lower production p99 read latency, 1 TB versus 3 TB of disk usage, and 45% to 50% lower cost per node. By Leela Kumili
